trust_decision.summary: DOM.sanitize is trusted to return HTML containing no script-executing attribute. It does not: removeAttributes iterates the live NamedNodeMap from elem.attributes while calling elem.removeAttribute, so the attribute immediately after every removed one is never examined; the survivor is then serialized back out by html.innerHTML and inserted as attribution HTML.

landing_point.why: The summary names DOM.sanitize(), and the skip happens in its private attribute-removal loop; an engineer reads dom.ts:109-138 first.

fix_sites.entry_point: AttributionControl: new AttributionControl({customAttribution}) and source.attribution from the style/TileJSON, both rendered by _updateAttributions() -> DOM.sanitize() -> _innerContainer.innerHTML
fix_sites.module_kind: DOM utility helper (private static of the DOM class, reached only from the attribution control)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only other HTML-string insertion into the map UI, Popup.setHTML (src/ui/popup.ts:463-475), carries an explicit API contract that it performs no filtering or sanitization (src/ui/popup.ts:446-448), so a solver can argue all non-attribution HTML paths are outside the sanitizer's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Attributions are legitimately HTML: the default customAttribution is an anchor link, and sources often ship and markup. An over-broad fix that strips every attribute, escapes all HTML or drops non-text elements breaks the documented default and the existing tests that expect and to survive with only the dangerous attributes removed.

O6_input_shapes: two consecutive dangerous attributes on one element (onload then ontoggle)
a dangerous attribute immediately following a removed one (href="javascript:..." then onclick)
dangerous attributes interleaved with harmless ones, and repeated dangerous attribute names on the same element
attribution text supplied as a single string or as an array joined with ' | ' (src/ui/control/attribution_control.ts:128-137,171)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: make clean() also drop dangerous child elements (iframe/object/embed/template), the same remove-while-iterating skip appears one level up because clean() walks html.children, a live HTMLCollection
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: clean() already recurses over element children and an element blocklist next to the attribute blocklist is the natural next hardening step

O8b_injection_room.sibling: route Popup.setHTML through DOM.sanitize for untrusted content, giving a second caller of the sanitizer in a different module
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Popup.setHTML is the other HTML-string API in the public surface and the docs already steer users toward sanitization

O8b_injection_room.sibling: extend isPossiblyDangerous with more URL-bearing attribute names (srcdoc, formaction, object data), needing a normalised-name lookup the current blocklist lacks
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the current list is only src/href/xlink:href and every sanitizer hardening starts by widening it

O9_family: DOM-based cross-site scripting (CWE-79): incomplete HTML attribute sanitizer caused by mutating a live NamedNodeMap during iteration

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm; vitest 4 unit config with jsdom environment; vite/rolldown bundling
O10_build.project_tests: src/util/dom.test.ts (six sanitize tests at the pinned commit) and src/ui/control/attribution_control.test.ts:366-374; run with `npm run test-unit` (vitest.config.unit.ts, jsdom, no WebGL needed for these)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: rewrite the loop as an index-based `for (let i = 0; i < elem.attributes.length; i++)`, which looks fixed but still skips the attribute that shifts into slot i after a removal
